question.problem: Find the angle between $a=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 0 \\ 6\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Rearranging the dot product formula, we have: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,a\,||\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}}\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8\cdot 3+0\cdot 6+6\cdot (-2)}{\sqrt{{8}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{6}^{2}}\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{6}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{12}{\sqrt{100}\cdot \sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{12}{10\cdot 7} \\  & =\frac{6}{35}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{6}{35})≈{80.13}^{∘}.
$$
